newsitem.title: CHINA: China capital housing plan faces space, water woe.
newsitem.headline: China capital housing plan faces space, water woe.

text.p: An ambitious plan by China's capital Beijing to build more housing is being held back by a shortage of space and utility services, the Xinhua news agency said on Wednesday.
Planners in Beijing were hoping to build housing on more than 40 square km (15 sq miles) to try to raise the average per capita living space to 16.5 sq m (178 sq ft) by 2010, Xinhua said.
Officials had already designated about 20 sq km (7.7 sq miles) of land for new housing, of which 10.55 sq km (4.1 sq miles) was under development, the agency said.
However, areas in the crowded city centre had no room for housing projects while the less dense suburban districts would have difficulty supplying water to new residences, Xinhua said.
The water table in some areas was nearly dry and increased demand on wells would cause the ground to sink, it said.
Authorities were counting on water diversion and pipeline projects to help quench the thirst of future residents, it said but gave no further details.
Average per capita living space in urban areas throughout China was 7.9 sq m (85 sq ft) in 1995, according to official figures.
Beijing's population has been estimated at around 10 million people.
